title: Chunk
description: A derived, retrievable chunk of a document. Chunks preserve parent-child relationships and provenance (ordinal, section path, character offsets) and record the embedding model + dimensions so vectors can be regenerated deterministically. Chunks are rebuildable derived artifacts, not canonical source-of-truth. Canonical shape from the Synapse design report; produced by the ingestion pipeline and consumed by hybrid retrieval.

doc_id.description: Identifier of the parent document this chunk was derived from.

tenant_id.description: Owning tenant/organization (inherited from the parent document; enforced via row-level security).

ordinal.description: Zero-based position of the chunk within the parent document, used for ordering and adjacency expansion.

section_path.description: Hierarchical section headings locating the chunk within the document structure.

examples: Reconcile outstanding journal entries before lock.

token_count.description: Number of tokens in the chunk under the ingestion tokenizer.

char_start.description: Inclusive character offset of the chunk start within the source document.

char_end.description: Exclusive character offset of the chunk end within the source document.

embedding_model.description: Identifier of the embedding model used to vectorize the chunk. Stamped so vectors can be rebuilt/explained.

embedding_dimensions.description: Dimensionality of the chunk's embedding vector.

vector_ref.description: Reference to the chunk's dense vector in the vector index (pgvector or external store).

sparse_terms_ref.description: Reference to the chunk's sparse/lexical term representation (e.g. BM25) for hybrid retrieval.

metadata.description: Free-form provenance metadata (stored as JSONB), e.g. document version and PII flags. Additional properties are allowed.
